items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Milford Piron, my teacher. Armand Piron.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. Lots of musicians in. Lots of musicians. Who were some of the other ones that you... What were the other ones that you...

Well, uh... Milford Piron, my teacher. Armand Piron. Thank you. Louis Cottrell's daddy. Bonnie Bigard, the Teos. Lorenzo Junior, Lorenzo Senior. Big I, Louis. Well, we could just go on and name quite a number of them. Piku.
The guys your age, how many of them are there? Let's see.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: See, Piran, you confine yourself to what was happening here in New Orleans.

ctx.x: Well, those guys could think so fast. Right. The Thaukes fans. They had a terrific ear and they could think fast. That's right. They had all the feeling. Well, now, when I listened to Trent's band, it doesn't sound the same as Piran's band. Did you have any band that sounded at all like, say, Piran's band did?

In the Texas area? In the Texas area? No, because they, they had a different way of playing music. Mm-hmm. See, Piran, you confine yourself to what was happening here in New Orleans. Mm-hmm. And these fellas in Texas, uh, they weren't familiar with the musician from, from New Orleans, or from Louisiana, I'd say. Uh, maybe just a few, one, two a year. Mm-hmm. It's not enough to patent that. Yeah. So, that, that type of music was built on a different type of feeling.
Well, stock arrangements was stock arrangements. That's right. But, uh, when I hear a band today playing stocks from, say, 1915, every band that plays them, plays them a little different.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: Because I had a cousin down there, Armand Pierron, which I have one of his numbers here

ctx.x: Oh yes, down there. Way down in the bottom.

Where Spanish people know that. That's right. Then I played with him on a couple of the trucks down there. And when I had gone back on a visit to New Orleans. And Piku and I were great friends. Because I had a cousin down there, Armand Pierron, which I have one of his numbers here that Crawford sent me in one of his arrangements. This happens to be his number here that Crawford wants me to record for him. I know this is Alvin Piku. This is Piron in Bocage. Or Mama's Gone Goodbye. That's a great... That's a good…
I'm sure with your experience and the natural talent and the way you played, it wouldn't be hard to come back. That's right.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: Piron is cousin, Armand Piron is cousin to me through marriage.

ctx.x: Was Milford Piron akin to AJ?
That's AJ's older brother. I see. Piron is cousin, Armand Piron is cousin to me through marriage.
Well Dick said to tell you that Bill Phillips is a bass drummer now with the Young Tuxedo Brass Band.
